question: Can the two matched local obstructions be detected from native cover equations and generic section words, without the characteristic-zero intersection polynomial?
selection: The same three frozen lattice-selected translates and the same native triple. Fix primes 53 and 61 from the preceding certified obstructions, plus 73 as a successful calibration prime. The detector receives only generic equations, primitive quadratic cover forms, their exact rational square scalings, and the selected generic words. No original characteristic-zero intersection result, exceptional point, rational parameter, or observed rank is passed to the detector.
geometry_gate: Require integral coefficients at p, the original discriminant of degree24 squarefree modulo p, smooth original infinity fibre, and three degree-two squarefree cover branch polynomials with pairwise disjoint branch divisors disjoint from the original discriminant. Verify all section and lift identities modulo p. Failure leaves that prime UNKNOWN.
method: Enumerate every fibre of the proper three-conic carrier above P1(Fp), including infinity and cover branch points. Evaluate all square-root choices in the weighted native polynomial maps. Compute each generic translate from the specialized published basis. Test P_A-P_B+P_D=S in the smooth group of the Weierstrass fibre, including nonsingular points on nodal fibres. No rational-function elimination or characteristic-zero factorization is used. A complete empty set gives a local solubility obstruction by proper reduction.
failure_semantics: A missed affine chart, bad geometry gate, singular image point or invalid group operation prevents exclusion. Nonempty reduction is only a necessary condition for a Qp point, and is not a rational point or rank certificate. The comparisons are retrospective and do not validate new cover-triple selection.
boundary: An equation-only necessary global-solubility test for specified relation constructions. It neither excludes the original fibre nor changes active search policy.
